transcription.notes: The document is the experimental-round answer sheet with the official answers overlaid in red boxes; competition, year and round are not printed on it (catalogue: IOM 2020, experiment). No points are printed anywhere. The pictures on pages 1, 2, 3 and the answer schematics on pages 4, 5, 6, 9, 11 carry the official answers (red arrows and boxes), so they are attached as solution figures; the unannotated photographs and setup schematics (pages 4, 5, 6, 8, 10) are statement figures. The shared data tables of page 17 are in paper.documentNotes (used by Questions 12-15). Page 21 (Additional forms 4) is blank graph paper. Printed values kept verbatim: Answer 2 prints 'Angles: 41 and 221' with the remark 'the sum is 180 deg (179-181)' although the two angles differ by 180; Answer 12 d) prints the ranges of A as '10-9…19-8', '10-8…19-7', '10-7…19-6' (the '19' is presumably 10); Answer 13 prints '0, 46-0,47' with a space; answers mix decimal points and commas and the unit 'нм' and 'см' in Cyrillic, as printed. No answer is printed for Q.6 d). Answer 6 c) prints the misspelling 'Verlically' (kept as printed: the mechanical check treats the capitalised word as a name) and gives a vertical direction for the horizontal stripe, as printed. The solution comment of Answer 15 d) is printed in Russian. Part labels use a Cyrillic 'с' in 'Q.14 с)' and 'Q.15 с)' in the print; written with Latin c here.

problems.statement: Which of the images (1 and 2) is formed by ordinary rays, and which by extraordinary?

solution.statement:
An image that rotates around a stationary one is created by extraordinary rays. Immobile - with ordinary rays. The still image -- by ordinary rays.

Answer 1

Ordinary 2

Extraordinary 1

parts.label: Q.12 d)
parts.statement:
The dependence of the second harmonic power on the first harmonic power can be expressed as follows, $I_{2\omega} = A \cdot I_{\omega}^{B}$.

From the experimental data, calculate the power $B$ to which you need to raise the power of the first harmonic to get a result proportional to the power of the second harmonic. Also calculate the proportionality factor $A$.

solution.statement:
Answer 12 a)

KDP 0.5 cm 0.107 %, 0,09 - 0,11% - OK

KDP 2.0 cm 1.51943 %, 1,43 - 1,52%- OK

KDP 4.0 cm 2.787%, 2,7 – 2,8%- OK

The main thing is to count at maximum power. $\frac{P_{max}(2\omega)}{P_{max}(\omega)} \cdot 100\%$

Answer 12 b)

KDP 0.5 cm Yes

KDP 2.0 cm Yes

KDP 4.0 cm Yes

For all crystals, conversion efficiency $< 10\%$

Answer 12 c) $P_{2\omega} \sim P_{\omega}^{2}$

parts.label: Q.14 a)
parts.statement: Using the experimental data on the dependence of the second harmonic power on the first harmonic power for all crystals, plot the dependence of the second harmonic power on the crystal length for the same maximum possible power of the first harmonic.

parts.label: Q.14 b)
parts.statement: Can this dependence of the second harmonic power on the crystal length be expressed in terms of a power function? If possible, indicate the degree.

parts.label: Q.14 c)
parts.statement: Briefly describe the reason why the experimental dependence of the second harmonic power on the crystal length differs from the theoretical one. Write down the answer in English.

answer.value: This is due to the laser beam divergence.

solution.statement:
Answer 14 a)

You need to plot somewhere all three graphs P (2w) versus P (w). Understand that you need to take the power P (2w) with the same power and maximum possible power P (w).

Plot the dependence of P (w) on L. And it is best on a double logarithmic scale.

There is also a point (0, 0) on the linear scale. There are only three crystals (0.5, 2 and 4 cm), but nobody canceled zero. It can be seen that this is not a power dependence.

On a logarithmic scale (even if there is no zero point), it is obvious that this is not a power dependence.

Answer 14 b) No

From the previous logarithmic graph, you can see that it is impossible.

Answer 14 c) This is due to the laser beam divergence. The divergence width of the laser beam is comparable to the phase matching width for crystals of 2 and 4 cm. Therefore, not all of the beam energy is converted equally effectively into SH. Theory is for plane waves. The longer the crystal, the more it differs from theory.

parts.label: Q.15 a)
parts.statement: What function of the power of the first harmonic should be proportional to the power of the third harmonic theoretically? Write down the formula.

parts.label: Q.15 b)
parts.statement: What function of the second harmonic power should be proportional to the third harmonic power theoretically? Write down the formula.

parts.label: Q.15 c)
parts.statement:
The dependence of the third harmonic power on the first harmonic power or the second harmonic power can be expressed as follows, $I_{3\omega} = A \cdot I_{\omega}^{B}$ or $I_{3\omega} = A \cdot I_{2\omega}^{B}$

From the experimental data, calculate the power $B$ to which you need to raise the power of the first harmonic to get a result proportional to the power of the third harmonic. Also calculate the proportionality factor $A$.

parts.label: Q.15 d)
parts.statement: From the experimental data, calculate the power B to which you need to raise the power of the second harmonic to get a result proportional to the power of the third harmonic. Also calculate the proportionality factor A.

parts.label: Q.15 e)
parts.statement: Briefly describe the reason why the experimental dependences of the third harmonic power on the first and second harmonics power do not coincide with the theoretical ones. Write down the answer in English.

answer.value: The filter transmits radiation of the fundamental and second harmonics.

solution.statement:
Answer 15 a) $P_{3\omega} \sim P_{\omega}^{3}$ Cubic dependence

Answer 15 b) $P_{3\omega} \sim P_{2\omega}^{3/2}$ Degree «one and a half»

Answer 15 c)

for $I_{3\omega} = A \cdot I_{\omega}^{B}$ $A = 10^{-10}\ldots 10^{-9}$ $B = 2.38..$ $2 < B < 3$

The main thing is that B is less than 3, but more than 2

Answer 15 d)

The main thing is that B is less than 1.5, but more than 1

for $I_{3\omega} = A \cdot I_{2\omega}^{B}$ $A = 10^{-2}\ldots10^{-1}$ $B = 1.2..$ $1 < B < 1.5$

Построить зависимости в двойном логарифмическом масштабе. Провести линию (т.е. выявить наклон) и вычислить степень. Учитывая неточность построений. Величины коэффициентов A не так важны. Важен порядок величины. См. дополнительные листы.

Answer 15 e) The video showed that when we remove the crystal for 3w, then a signal remains on the photodetector 3. When we close 3 FP, then the signal is less, when we open, then more. This means that either w or 2w radiation passes through the filter, which should be absorbed.

The filter transmits radiation of the fundamental and second harmonics.
